newsitem.title: UK: Specials still in demand on UK gilt repo market.
newsitem.headline: Specials still in demand on UK gilt repo market.

text.p: Trading on the UK gilt repo market again centred on the same three special stocks that have held centre stage recently, but some incipient interest was also noted in what is expected to be the next auction stock.
The 8.0 percent gilts due 2001 were quoted at 5.20 percent for overnight, around 50 basis points below general collateral (GC) levels.
The 6.0s of 1999 were put at similar levels but attracted less demand, while the 7.0 percent gilts due 2001 were bid at around 5.0 percent.
"It's still the same three, but they're perhaps not quite as special as they have been on recent occasions," one trader said.
With the cash market also enjoying a quiet day as a modest 850 million stg shortage was fully taken out, there was little to add excitement to the gilt repo market.
"Cash had a comfortable day and period rates were much as they were," a trader said.
Overnight GC was last quoted at around 5.25 percent.
Traders said the 8.0 percent gilts due 2021, which are expected to be the next Bank of England auction stock, were being talked about at levels around 30 to 40 points below GC.
"Last week they were starting to get a little bit more wanted at 30 to 40 basis points under GC levels over the period covering the auction," one trader said.
"Today I don't think there has been much business, but those are still the levels people are suggesting."
Details of the auction stock will be announced on September 17 and the auction is on September 25.
Reflecting the easy tone, overnight cash was quoted as low as 2-1/2 percent in late business, well below Monday's levels around 5-13/16 3/4.
One-week money was at 5-3/4 11/16 and one-month at 5-3/4 23/32 percent.
